items.title: Sticks and their labels are cut off on the 844px baseline
items.what: In the pre-fight and in-fight screenshots (2, 3, 10, 11) the STANCE/TECHNIQUE sticks begin around y=810 and their 'STANCE'/'TECHNIQUE' labels sit around y=1030-1060. On the stated 390x844 baseline the sticks are visible for only ~34px and the labels are entirely off-screen.
items.why: A touch-first karate game whose player cannot see which stick is stance and which is technique loses reliable input at the exact moment it matters, and the unlabeled sticks invite wrong-thumb taps.
items.how: Bind the bottom stack (moves panel + sticks + labels) to viewport height so it fits 844px: raise the sticks to roughly 690-880 and keep labels at ~900-940, or shrink the sticks so the full circle plus label fits. Treat 'Large controls' as an in-bounds option, not the default.

items.title: Loading bar shows no visible progress
items.what: Screenshot 1: the bar under 'Downloading the game' is a ~2px dark hairline against the near-black background, with no fill, percentage, or animation anywhere on it.
items.why: This is the player's first 5 seconds with the product. With no feedback, a download that takes seconds feels frozen and players will reload or close, hurting retention and making ShoeMoney's branded moment wasted.
items.how: Fill the bar with the warm gold accent used on the FIGHT button, add a subtle shimmer or tick animation, and append a percentage or 'Downloading… N%' line so progress is legible at a glance.

items.title: Game runs unfixed in landscape and the layout stretches
items.what: Screenshot 9 shows the dojo rendered in landscape: the fighters shrink to the middle ~40% of frame height, the dojo columns and tatami stretch horizontally, and the STANCE/TECHNIQUE sticks sit at the extreme bottom corners with their labels lost in the black bar.
items.why: A phone twin-stick in landscape puts both sticks beyond comfortable thumb reach and shrinks the fighters, so hit read, timing, and touch accuracy all degrade; the warm cinematic composition is also broken.
items.how: Lock the viewport to portrait (screen.orientation.lock('portrait')). If landscape must be tolerated, letterbox it and scale the fighters to fill the short axis instead of stretching the generated backdrop.

items.title: Sticks and FIGHT button stay live during the countdown
items.what: Screenshots 2 and 15 show 'STARTING IN 2' / 'STARTING IN 4' with the FIGHT button still on screen and the full STANCE/TECHNIQUE sticks active below it.
items.why: A player mashing stance or technique during the countdown enters the bout out of their intended setup, or triggers a stray move before the exchange begins; it punishes early engagement instead of rewarding it.
items.how: Disable both sticks and dim the FIGHT button until the countdown hits zero, then start the bout with a brief 'GO' flash so the first input is intentional.

items.title: Moves hint panel stays up during the bout
items.what: Screenshots 3, 4, 10, 11: the STANCE/TECHNIQUE key-hint panel (step/jump/crouch, back/forward/up/down) remains visible during live play, occupying ~60-70px directly above the sticks.
items.why: It adds visual noise over the combat zone during exchanges and, on the baseline phone, pushes the already-overflowing controls further off-screen, compounding the bottom-stack problem.
items.how: Auto-dismiss the panel after the first round or on the first clean landing, and add a small toggle to recall it; keep it hidden by default during combat.
